title: Context-aware release allocator for safe percentage ramps and cohort staleness handling
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: build a context-aware release allocator that performs percentage traffic ramps and cohort assignments while accounting for cohort staleness, recent regression signals, and compatibility constraints. The allocator should enable time-windowed canaries, safety gate checkpoints, an automated rollback scorer, and a manual 'circuit-halt' override. This ticket covers design, a simulation harness, a small runtime controller, and observability hooks needed to operate the system in production.
acceptance_criteria: Allocator can perform staged percentage ramps (0% -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) driven by configurable windows and metrics
Cohort assignment honors attribute-based selectors (region, tier, user-seg) and applies a staleness penalty to long-idle cohorts
Automatic rollback scorer triggers a halt and rollback when combined metric score exceeds configured thresholds
Dry-run simulation reproduces rollout plan with synthetic traffic and emits the same scoring decisions as controller
Dashboard exposes per-cohort latency, error-rate, regression-score, and allocation history for at least 30 days
Manual circuit-halt button in Console prevents further ramps and publishes an incident note to the channel
implementation_notes: Design a scoring function that blends relative latency change (p50/p95 deltas), error-rate increase, and model quality regression (where available) into a single numeric 'regression_score'
Create a 'staleness_penalty' factor computed from cohort activity histogram; cohorts inactive >72h get a configurable penalty applied to allocation probability
Controller will use a stepper policy with backoff: if a checkpoint fails, pause for N minutes, then either retry at same percentage or step back depending on severity
Compatibility checks: verify model variant, KV cache schema, and tokenizer fingerprint before first cohort promotion
Rollout state persisted in central store with versioned changelog to enable replay and postmortem debugging
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring function with edge cases (zero-traffic cohorts, noisy telemetry, missing quality metrics)
Integration test that runs a full ramp in staging against synthetic traffic and validates rollback behavior
Chaos experiment: induce elevated tail latency in a promoted cohort and assert controller halts and rolls back within configured SLA
Regression test ensuring existing canary APIs (traffic-weight, cohort selectors) are backward compatible
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): deploy controller as a sidecar to canary infra; dry-run for 72h with synthetic traffic
Phase 2 (internal): enable 0.5% internal traffic split for 24h; verify telemetry and scoring matches simulation
Phase 3 (limited public): ramp to 5% over 4 hours with 30m checkpoint windows; enable automatic rollback scorer
Phase 4 (wide): after 48h of stable signals, promote to 100% and mark LTS promotion eligibility if model variant passes compatibility gates
telemetry_queries: alert if regression_score > 0.7 for two consecutive windows or p95 latency increases > 30%
